record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For an n-vertex graph G and a specified vertex of G, construct an exact counting algorithm running in O*(1.99^n) time that counts the number of cycles passing through the specified vertex, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Count the number of cycles through a given vertex in G.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $v\in V$ be a specified vertex. A cycle through $v$ is a simple cycle of $G$ that contains $v$. Design a deterministic (or randomized) exact algorithm that, given $G$ and $v$, outputs the exact number of simple cycles of $G$ that pass through $v$, and runs in time $O^*(1.99^n)$, where $O^*(\cdot)$ suppresses factors polynomial in $n$. Equivalently, exhibit a constant $c<2$ and an exact counting algorithm achieving running time $O^*(c^n)$ for this problem.
artifact.status_search_result: No source clearly establishes an $O^*(c^n)$ exact counting algorithm with $c<2$ for the number of simple cycles through a specified vertex in a general graph. Related work on counting Hamiltonian cycles achieves $2^{n-\Omega(\sqrt n)}$ time (Björklund–Kaski–Williams and subsequent improvements), which is $O^*(2^n)$ up to subexponential factors but not $O^*(c^n)$ for a constant $c<2$. The status of breaking the $2^n$ barrier for this counting problem appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Computing Permanents and Counting Hamiltonian Cycles Faster
status_evidence.snippet: Counting Hamiltonian cycles in n-vertex graphs in time 2^{n-Omega(sqrt n)}, improving earlier 2^{n-Omega(sqrt n / log log n)} bound.
status_evidence.claim: Best known counting algorithms for related cycle-counting problems remain at 2^{n-o(n)}, not O^*(c^n) with c<2.
